question: Should ClawHub/OpenClaw still support the legacy `molt.bot/install.sh` path, or should it be explicitly redirected or retired in favor of supported install commands?
rationale: The observable failure is outside the tracked ClawHub source tree, so automation cannot choose whether to patch, redirect, or retire the legacy hosted installer without maintainer intent.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
options.body: Treat `molt.bot/install.sh` as a legacy alias and direct users to supported OpenClaw/ClawHub install paths with the current Node support range.

options.title: Support and harden it
options.body: Bring the hosted installer source under traceable ownership and fix the cleanup glob/npm retry path with a macOS Homebrew zsh reproduction.

options.title: Keep waiting for reporter data
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on a fresh reproduction if maintainers cannot yet decide ownership of the hosted installer.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
recommendation.body: Treat `molt.bot/install.sh` as a legacy alias and direct users to supported OpenClaw/ClawHub install paths with the current Node support range.

likelyOwner.reason: The current maintained CLI/package and install-guidance surfaces blame to Patrick-Erichsen, making them the best available routing owner for the support-boundary decision.
